entries.abstract: Let $A,B\subset\mathbb{Z}_p$ be nonempty with $|A|\neq|B|$, and let $A\rplus B$ be the set of sums $a+b$ with $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and $a\neq b$. Alon, Nathanson and Ruzsa proved $|A\rplus B|\ge\min\{p,|A|+|B|-2\}$. Liu and Qian conjectured that when $|A|+|B|\le p$ equality forces $A$ and $B$ to be arithmetic progressions with a common difference, with $B$ the first or the last $|B|$ terms of $A$. We refute the conjecture. For every prime $p\ge11$ there is a critical pair with $|A|+|B|=p$, $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ and neither set an arithmetic progression, and for $p=13$ one with $|A|+|B|=p-2$. These pairs satisfy $|A|+2|B|\ge p+2$, and the inequality $|A+B|\le|A\rplus B|+|A\cap B|$ shows that no counterexample can do better. We conjecture that every critical pair with $|A|+2|B|\le p+1$ is arithmetic, and prove this when $|A+B|=|A|+|B|-1$. In the conjectured range the statement is equivalent to the minimality of the ordinary sumset, to a defect of one element, and to the emptiness of the band $|A|+|B|\le|A+B|\le p-1$. We also describe all critical pairs with $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ at $p=|A|+2|B|-2$, and prove that every critical pair satisfies $|A\cap(A+t)|\ge|A|-|B|$ for $t\in B-B$ and that one with a uniquely represented restricted sum is arithmetic whenever all critical pairs with a smaller second set are.

entries.name: On intersection forms of spin $4$-manifolds with AR homology sphere boundary
entries.abstract: In this paper, building on the work of Dai--Sasahira--Stoffregen, we derive constraints on the intersection forms of smooth, compact, indefinite, spin $4$-manifolds bounded by almost-rational plumbed homology spheres (AR homology spheres) using two methods. First, we use the constraints on the existence of $\operatorname{Pin}(2)$-equivariant maps between representation spheres, established by Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu in their proof of the $10/8 + 4$-inequality. Second, we compute Lin's $κo$-invariant for AR homology spheres. Combined with Lin's version of the relative $10/8$-inequality, this computation yields constraints different from those based on Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu. As applications, we give an alternative proof of the non-sliceness of the $(2n, 1)$-cables of the figure-eight knot for even $n$---a result originally proved by Kang, Park, and Taniguchi via real Seiberg--Witten theory---by showing within ordinary Seiberg--Witten theory that certain cyclic branched covers of them are nontrivial in the homology cobordism group. We also obtain new lower bounds on the minimal genus of surfaces in various $4$-manifolds bounded by knots whose double branched covers are AR homology spheres. Moreover, we provide an obstruction to smooth $4$-manifold decompositions related to the $11/8$-conjecture.

entries.name: Determining $W^{1,n}$ conductivities for Calderón's problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$
entries.abstract: We establish a global uniqueness result at the critical Sobolev regularity for the isotropic Calderón problem in all dimensions $n \ge 4$. More precisely, for every $n \ge 4$ and every bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, any real-valued, uniformly elliptic scalar conductivity $γ\in W^{1,n}(Ω)$ is uniquely determined by its full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. Together with the known results for $n=2,3,4$ in the literature, this settles a long-standing open problem in the field while providing a unified proof for all dimensions $n \ge 4$. To prove uniqueness at this endpoint, we develop an averaged trace norm method, which combines complex geometrical optics with trace-norm estimates averaged over directions.

entries.name: A Dubnov-Ivanov-Nagata-Higman Theorem for NIP nilrings
entries.abstract: We prove that NIP nilrings of bounded nilexponent are nilpotent. We also deduce that NIP $ω$-categorical $n$-Engel Lie algebras of characteristic $p>n$ are nilpotent, yielding a case of the Lie algebra analogous of Wilson conjecture for $ω$-categorical groups.

entries.name: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions associated with polynomial sequences satisfying a first-order differential recurrence. As applications, we prove weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials, several families of Eulerian polynomials, the Bell polynomials, and the reflected generalized Laguerre polynomials. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai concerning the Bell and Laguerre polynomials.

entries.name: The Dimension Conjecture for Hypersurfaces Is True
entries.abstract: The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for arbitrary real-analytic hypersurfaces. More precisely, for $N\ge2$ the dimension of the Lie algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ of the indicated class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This is exactly the dimension of the corresponding algebra for any Levi-nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric. For a finitely nondegenerate hypersurface with constant positive Levi rank $r$ satisfying $0<r<N-1$, the sharper bound $N^2+r+1=N^2+N-m$ is obtained, where $m=N-1-r$. We also establish the sharper bound $N^2+N-1$ for the automorphism algebra of a nonspherical holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface; consequently, dimensions $N^2+N,...,N^2+2N-1$ cannot occur (a dimension gap).

entries.name: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
entries.abstract: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

entries.name: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
entries.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

entries.name: Perdomo's index conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres
entries.abstract: Let $x:M^n\to\sphere^{n+1}(1)$, $n\ge2$, be a full minimal immersion of a closed, connected, oriented manifold. We prove that its Morse index is at least $n+3$, with equality precisely for the standard Clifford embeddings. For a non-Clifford image, the constant function and the position and normal coordinates span a space containing an $(n+4)$-dimensional subspace on which the Jacobi quadratic form is negative definite. Thus we resolve Perdomo's index conjecture.

entries.name: Log-concavity of rank and crank statistics for integer partitions
entries.abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang [Adv. Math. 2021] conjectured that $M(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$, and that $N(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge73$ and $|m|\le n-73$. In this paper, we prove these two conjectures.

entries.name: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
entries.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

entries.name: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
entries.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $ξ$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $ζ$ of $p$ such that $ |ξ-ζ|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.The Lean 4 formalization of the main results are also provided.

entries.name: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
entries.abstract: We study the structural dimension of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

entries.name: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
entries.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link which is not Lorenz, thereby disproving the Birman--Kofman conjecture that every horseshoe link is a Lorenz link. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

entries.name: Maximality of the Došen-Petrić Boolean Category
entries.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

entries.name: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
entries.abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

entries.name: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
entries.abstract: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

entries.name: Abelian varieties with homotheties
entries.abstract: In 1980, Bogomolov proved that the $\ell$-adic Galois image of an Abelian variety over a number field contains an open subgroup of the homotheties. In 1986, Serre refined that result, showing that the homotheties coming from the Galois side were uniformly bounded in $\ell$ inside the homotheties of the codomain of the representation. In a 2007 paper, Zarhin shows that Bogomolov's conclusion can fail in non-trivial cases for global function fields. We prove a suitable analogue of Serre's results over finitely generated fields of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we prove a new case of the 1978 conjecture by Geyer and Jarden.

entries.name: A Burns-Krantz theorem on convex domains
entries.abstract: We prove two boundary rigidity theorems for holomorphic self-maps of bounded convex domains. Let $Ω\subset\C^n$, $n\geq1$, and suppose that $\partialΩ$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $p\in\partialΩ$ for some $0<α\leq1$. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ satisfies $f(z)=z+o(|z-p|^3)$ as $z\to p$ in one fixed non-tangential approach region at $p$, then $f=\id_Ω$. We also prove a rigidity theorem for bounded convex domains $Ω$ without assuming boundary smoothness. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ of $Ω$ satisfies $f(z)-z=O(|z-p|^m)$ as $z\to p\in\partialΩ$ for some $m>1+2π/θ_p$, where $θ_p$ is the supremum of sector angles in the open tangent cone at $p$, taken over complex lines through its vertex, then $f=\id_Ω$, which proves a conjecture of Zimmer.

entries.name: On (Pathwidth, Clique)-boundedness
entries.abstract: We prove that every $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class of graphs has bounded tree-independence number, answering a question of Bešter Štorgel, Dallard, Lozin, Milanič, and Zamaraev. We deduce this from a bound on the tree-independence number of graphs with neither $\B_ρ$ nor $K_{σ,σ}$ as an induced minor, where $\B_ρ$ is the complete binary tree of height $ρ$ and the bound depends only on $ρ$ and $σ$. We then obtain an asymptotically sharp bound on the path-independence number of $n$-vertex graphs in any $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class. The lower-bound examples also give counterexamples to a conjecture of Hickingbotham and Joret. We further prove that, for every forest $F$ and every $\ell\in\N$, there is a constant $k=k(F,\ell)\in\N$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced theta or $\ell$-long prism and no induced subgraph isomorphic to $F$ satisfies tree-independence number at most $k$. This proves a strengthened form of a conjecture of Chudnovsky, Hajebi, and Trotignon. Finally, for every integer $s\ge2$, we characterize the forests $F$ for which excluding $F$ as an induced minor and $K_{s,s}$ as an induced subgraph bounds tree-independence number. This extends the characterization of Bonnet, Duhamel, and Hickingbotham, who considered bounded pathwidth with $K_{s,s}$ excluded as a subgraph.

entries.name: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
entries.abstract: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

entries.name: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
entries.abstract: Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value. For matrices of odd order, the sharp cardinality bound was already established by Delsarte and Goethals (1975). In this paper, we prove the Cooperstein conjecture for matrices of even order and, more generally, we prove its additive analogue by determining, for all admissible parameters, the maximum size of an additive subgroup of alternating matrices in which every nonzero matrix has at least the prescribed rank. Our proof uses Pfaffian equations to characterize alternating matrices of rank below the prescribed minimum. We study the minimal graded free resolutions of the corresponding Pfaffian rings. The Cohen--Macaulay property and the $a$-invariant of each Pfaffian ring determine the largest shift in its resolution. We use trace functions on evaluation quotients to construct polynomial indicators for the matrices of small rank in an additive subgroup. The largest shift controls their degrees, yielding the upper bound by a counting argument. Finally, we give explicit trace constructions attaining the bound.

entries.name: Nonlinear syzygies in ordinary powers of chordal cover ideals
entries.abstract: We construct connected chordal graphs whose cover ideals have ordinary powers that are not componentwise linear over any field, disproving the Herzog--Hibi--Ohsugi conjecture.

entries.name: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
entries.abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we show $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjecture this for all prime powers.

entries.name: Exact and Approximate Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Multivariate Diffusions under High-Frequency Sampling
entries.abstract: We establish the asymptotic theory of the exact maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for discretely observed multivariate ergodic diffusions under high-frequency, long-span sampling, solving an open problem posed by \citet{YCW2019} and \citet{Li2013}. The drift may grow linearly, and the volatility is bounded away from zero and either bounded or proportional to $1+|x|$. When the sampling interval decays polynomially, the exact MLE is consistent, asymptotically normal and efficient, with rates $\sqrt{nΔ_n}$ for drift and $\sqrt n$ for diffusion parameters. Under an additional condition on ergodic averages, and when the time span $nΔ_n$ also grows polynomially, its moments converge as well. The proof never analyzes the exact likelihood directly: it shows that a closed-form density expansion of sufficiently high order is uniformly accurate in relative terms at every observed transition, so that the two log-likelihoods differ by $o_P(1)$ uniformly in the parameter. The same argument yields accuracy conditions under which an approximate likelihood is asymptotically equivalent to the exact one; in particular, the approximate MLE of Yang, Chen and Wan converges to the true parameter. For the delta-expansion estimator of fixed order $K\ge1$, we derive the leading bias explicitly. It shows that $nΔ_n^{K+1}\to0$ cannot be weakened when the bias constant is nonzero, and that the bias falls on the drift parameters for even $K$ and on the diffusion parameters for odd $K$. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the predicted biases.

entries.name: The minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for some k
entries.abstract: A graph on at least 2k+2 vertices is k-extendable if every matching of size k extends to a perfect matching, and it is minimally k-extendable if it is k-extendable but deleting any edge is not. Plummer proved that every k-extendable graph is (k+1)-connected. So its minimum degree is at least k+1. Lou and Yu conjectured that a minimally k-extendable graph on at most 4k vertices has minimum degree in {k+1,2k,2k+1}; the case k=1 and the claw-free case of k=2 have been settled previously. We determine the minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for k=2 and k=3, thereby settling the Lou--Yu conjecture for these two values. For k=2 the minimum degree is in {3,4,5}. For k=3 it is in {4,7} at orders 8 and 10, and in {4,6,7} at order 12. The proofs pass to the complement graph and combine Tutte's perfect matching theorem with a classification of four-vertex and six-vertex obstructions. All predicted values are realized by explicit constructions.

entries.name: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
entries.abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

entries.name: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
entries.abstract: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$. We prove that $a_k(n)\ge0$ for all $k,n\ge0$, thereby resolving a conjecture on signed odd-multiplicity partitions. Our proof combines a positive theta--MacMahon factorization for the generating functions restricted to odd part sizes with a dyadic product decomposition that extends positivity to arbitrary part sizes. Moreover, we establish strict positivity $a_k(n)>0$ for every $k\ge2$ and $n\ge\binom{k+1}{2}$.

entries.name: Global rigidity and the Hessian energy identity for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
entries.abstract: We prove that every entire classical stable solution of the one-phase Bernoulli problem in dimension five or six is one-dimensional. In dimensions three through six, we establish an exact interior identity for the scale-invariant Hessian energy of sequences with bounded Morse index. Hence, the global stability conjecture is solved.

entries.name: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$). We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit and Langlands correspondence is not needed for its description (it is a principle ideal, where the generator is given by some version of the discriminant function). We also prove our general conjecture for $G=\mathrm{SL}(2)$.

entries.name: An extremal question of Erdős et al. on cycles
entries.abstract: This paper addresses an extremal problem on long cycles proposed by Erdős, Faudree, Schelp and Simonovits in 1989. Let \(2\le k\le d<n\) be positive integers. For an n-vertex simple graph G, let \(θ_+^G\) count vertices of degree at least d, and \(C_{\ge k+1}\) denote a cycle of length at least \(k+1\). The original conjecture claimed that G contains a \(C_{\ge k+1}\) whenever \(θ_+^G \ge \lfloor k/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/d \rfloor+2\). Li, Ma and Ning disproved it with infinite counterexamples and gave linear lower bounds. Gan, Yi and Jiang later obtained piecewise sufficient conditions depending on the parity of k, whose bounds are sharp only when \(k=d\) and loose for \(k\ne d\). We derive a new sufficient condition for \(C_{\ge k+1}\). For odd \(k=d\), we use Woodall's sharp bound \(θ_+^G \ge k(n-2)/(2(k-1))+1\). For all other admissible parameters, our threshold is unified and independent of the parity of k: \(θ_+^G \ge \lfloor k/2 \rfloor (n-1)/d + (n-d-1)\lfloor k/2 \rfloor/(d(d-\lfloor k/2 \rfloor))+1\). We construct \(C_{\ge k+1}\)-free graphs to prove tightness for all admissible k. This resolves this long-standing Erdős-type extremal problem concerning high-degree vertices and long cycles.

entries.name: Moser--Trudinger inequalities and the complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation
entries.abstract: We study sharp Moser--Trudinger inequalities for the complex Monge--Ampère energy. On the unit ball, we determine the optimal energy coefficient and additive constant in the logarithmic Moser--Trudinger inequality. We deduce subcritical Moser--Trudinger inequalities in exponential form with explicit bounds proportional to $\varepsilon^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the relative distance to the critical coefficient. The proof establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness for the associated mean field equation by showing that every smooth solution has constant boundary normal derivative. This gives existence and uniqueness precisely for total masses $0<Λ<[2π(n+1)]^n$, proving Berman--Berndtsson's conjecture. We also establish smoothness of bounded pluripotential and finite-energy solutions. Domain monotonicity transfers the exponential estimates and the optimal logarithmic energy coefficient to bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains.

entries.name: Equivalence of Small and Large Quasi-kernels
entries.abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set which can reach every vertex of $D$ by a directed path of length at most 2. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex source-free digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q|\le n/2$, and the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]|\ge n/2$. Our main result shows for any $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$ an equivalence between the following two statements: \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex source-free digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |Q|\le n-Ω(n^β).\] \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |N^+[Q]|\ge Ω(n^{2-\frac{1}β}).\] That is, any sublinear bound for one problem is equivalent to a corresponding sublinear bound for the other. This combined with previous work establishing an equivalence for linear bounds shows that the two problems are largely equivalent to each other. We additionally give a slight refinement to the recent breakthrough of Rutschmann for these problems which, together with the result above, gives the best known bounds of $n-Ω(n^{3/4})$ and $Ω(n^{2/3})$ for the Small and Large Quasi-kernel Conjectures, respectively. Our proofs are due to ChatGPT's Astra 6; the writing is all our own.

entries.name: Minimum outdegree forcing directed cycles
entries.abstract: The Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture, one of the best known open problems on oriented graphs, asserts that every oriented graph on $n$ vertices with minimum outdegree at least $n/\ell$ contains a directed cycle of length at most $\ell$. Motivated by it, Kelly, Kühn and Osthus asked for the minimum degree condition that forces a directed cycle of length exactly $\ell$. The semidegree version of this problem was recently solved, but the methods used there rely on bounding the directed diameter, which requires control over the indegrees. In the setting of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture, where only the outdegrees are bounded, the answer was known only for $\ell$ not divisible by $3$. We determine the optimal minimum outdegree forcing a directed cycle of length $\ell$ for every sufficiently large $\ell$ and $n$. This establishes the outdegree version of the Kelly-Kühn-Osthus conjecture for all large $\ell$, up to a small correction of the additive term, which in general cannot be avoided.

entries.name: On Ext-groups between Arthur-type modules of the graded Hecke algebras of type A
entries.abstract: Let $\mathbb H_n$ be the graded Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. This article establishes a formula for Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and a $W$-type $\mathbb H_n$-module in terms of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain an explicit and efficient method to compute Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and an Arthur-type module of $\mathbb H_n$. In particular, this proves new instances of a conjecture of Chan and Prasad on Ext non-vanishing between Arthur-type representations. We also discuss some other non-Ext vanishing results for calibrated modules.

entries.name: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
entries.abstract: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A.Hanlon, J.Hicks, and O.Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

entries.name: On Green's Conjecture for Curves on Anticanonical Surfaces
entries.abstract: We prove Green's conjecture for smooth curves $C$ on rational surfaces $X$ such that $-K_X|_C$ is effective on $C$. In addition, on birationally ruled surfaces $X$ of irregularity $q \geq 1$ carrying an effective anticanonical divisor, we show that Green's conjecture holds for all smooth curves $C$ on $X$ covering the base curve with degree at least $2$, provided the latter has only finitely many gonal pencils or the gonality of $C$ is special with respect to the ruling.

entries.name: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
entries.abstract: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.

entries.name: Higher-Derivative Conjectures of Sendov
entries.abstract: We prove Conjectures~3 and~8 of Sendov's 2002 survey and deduce Conjecture~9. More precisely, let $p$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. For every integer $s$ with $1\le s<n$, we prove that each zero of $p$ lies within distance $2s/(s+1)$ of a zero of $p^{(s)}$. For quartics, we obtain the sharp bound $2/\sqrt3$ for the second derivative and determine all polynomials attaining it.

entries.name: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
entries.abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

entries.name: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
entries.abstract: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.

entries.name: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
entries.abstract: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

entries.name: General curves on smooth quadric hypersurfaces
entries.abstract: We prove a sharp existence theorem for non-degenerate maps from a general curve to a smooth quadric hypersurface, deforming in a smooth family of expected dimension. Along the way, we prove that if a general curve in projective space lies on a quadric (as dictated by the Maximal Rank Conjecture, now a theorem of E. Larson), then a general such quadric is smooth.

entries.name: Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs
entries.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.

papers.name: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.

papers.name: Greatest Common Divisors and an Unlikely Intersection Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove inequalities involving greatest common divisors of functions at integral points with respect to numerically parallel divisors, generalizing a result of Wang and Yasufuku (after work of Bugeaud-Corvaja-Zannier, Corvaja-Zannier, and the second author). In addition to proving results in a broader context than previously considered, we also study the exceptional set in this setting, for both the counting function and the proximity function. Based on our study of exceptional sets, we propose new conjectures connected to the topic of unlikely intersections. We prove special cases of the conjectures on abelian varieties and the algebraic torus, including a completely explicit result in the former case, and provide a link between the conjectures and exceptional sets for inequalities involving greatest common divisors.

papers.name: On non-isomorphic universal sofic groups
papers.abstract: We show that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ non-isomorphic universal sofic groups. This proves a conjecture of Simon Thomas.

papers.name: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
papers.abstract: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $ω$-ASD connections (where $ω$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

papers.name: Complexity Framework For Forbidden Subgraphs V: Beyond Simple Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate how allowing self-loops and multi-edges (i.e. moving from simple graphs to pseudographs) impacts the complexity of graph problems on finitely defined monotone graph classes. We do this by extending the C123-framework beyond simple graphs. We use several testbed problems to illustrate some of the new and varied behaviours introduced by the transition to pseudographs. We show that Pseudograph Matching Cut and Pseudograph d-Cut are C123-problems. Consequently, for every finite set HH of simple graphs, we obtain a complete complexity classification for these problems on HH-subgraph-free graphs. This sharply contrasts with their simple-graph counterparts, which are not C123-problems and their complexity remains open even for classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph H. We also show that Pseudograph Stable Cut is not a C123-problem. Nevertheless, for graph classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph, the problem mirrors the C123 classification; this correspondence already fails for sets of size 2. This gives the first example of a problem that aligns with C123-problems for a single forbidden subgraph but not for larger sets. Motivated by the interpretation of Stable Cut as a surjective homomorphism to a partially reflexive path, we also study surjective homomorphisms to partially reflexive cycles on k vertices with one irreflexive vertex. These problems share structural similarities with Pseudograph Stable Cut. We prove that for k at least 6, they are NP-complete on triangle-free pseudographs. However, unlike Pseudograph Stable Cut, they are polynomial-time solvable on all graph classes with bounded-degree.

papers.name: Finite element spaces of double forms
papers.abstract: The tensor product of two differential forms of degree $p$ and $q$ is a multilinear form that is alternating in its first $p$ arguments and alternating in its last $q$ arguments. These forms, which are known as double forms or $(p,q)$-forms, play a central role in certain differential complexes that arise when studying partial differential equations. We construct piecewise polynomial finite element spaces for all of the natural subspaces of the space of $(p,q)$-forms, excluding one subspace which fails to admit a piecewise constant discretization. As special cases, our construction recovers known finite element spaces for symmetric matrices with tangential-tangential continuity (the Regge finite elements), symmetric matrices with normal-normal continuity, and trace-free matrices with normal-tangential continuity. It also gives rise to new spaces, like a finite element space for tensors possessing the symmetries of the Riemann curvature tensor.

papers.name: First-order methods for stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization with deterministic constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization problems with deterministic constraints. Existing methods typically aim to find an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, in which both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are within a prescribed tolerance $ε$. However, in many practical applications, constraints must be nearly satisfied with certainty, rendering such solutions potentially unsuitable due to the risk of substantial violations. To address this issue, we propose stochastic first-order methods for finding an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, where the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$ and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. Our methods apply an accelerated stochastic gradient (ASG) scheme or a modified variance-reduced ASG scheme $only\ once$ to a sequence of quadratic penalty subproblems with appropriately chosen penalty parameters. We establish first-order oracle complexity bounds for the proposed methods in computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.name: Co-periods and central symmetric cube L-values
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the co-period integral attached to an automorphic form on $\GL(2)$ and two exceptional theta series on the cubic Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $\GL(2)$. In the local aspect, we show the $\Hom$-space is always of one dimension and conduct the unramified calculations. In the global aspect, we give the Euler decomposition for the co-period integrals of Eisenstein series and propose an Ichino-Ikeda type conjecture relating the co-period integrals of cuspidal forms to the central critical value of symmetric cube $L$-functions. We also deduce from the local multiplicity one result that there exist cuspidal automorphic forms with prescribed local components and non-vanishing central symmetric cube $L$-values.

papers.name: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.name: A Taxonomy of Numerical Differentiation Methods
papers.abstract: Differentiation is a cornerstone of computing and data analysis in every discipline of science and engineering. Indeed, most fundamental physics laws are expressed as relationships between derivatives in space and time. However, derivatives are rarely directly measurable and must instead be computed, often from noisy, potentially corrupt data streams. There is a rich and broad literature of computational differentiation algorithms, but many impose extra constraints to work correctly, e.g. periodic boundary conditions, or are compromised in the presence of noise and corruption. It can therefore be challenging to select the method best-suited to any particular problem. Here we review a broad range of numerical methods for calculating derivatives, present important contextual considerations and choice points, compare relative advantages, and provide basic theory for each algorithm in order to assist users with the mathematical underpinnings. This serves as a practical guide to help scientists and engineers match methods to application domains. We also provide an open-source Python package, PyNumDiff, which contains a broad suite of methods for differentiating noisy data.

papers.name: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
papers.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $ε$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

papers.name: Finite de Finetti for convex bodies and Polynomial Optimization
papers.abstract: We study polynomial optimization over convex bodies with separately affine objectives and local affine equality and inequality constraints. We construct a convergent hierarchy of conic relaxations with explicit finite-level error bounds of order $n^{-1/2}$ at level $n$, complemented by a constructive rounding scheme that produces feasible points. The relaxation bounds and rounded objective values bracket the optimum at the same rate. The analytic ingredient is a finite de Finetti representation theorem for arbitrary proper cones: bipartite marginals of symmetric extensions in maximal tensor products are $O(n^{-1/2})$-close, in base norm, to points of the minimal tensor product. Its proof combines a uniform, monogamy-type bound on a variational mutual information based on Frenkel's relative entropy with classical conditioning and informationally complete measurements. We apply the framework to the assemblage relaxation of two-player non-local games in general probabilistic theories. For polytopic state spaces, the hierarchy consists of linear programs, and experiments on the Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt (CHSH) game provide a numerical proof of concept for the outer approximations and feasible rounding procedure.

papers.name: Time-Delayed Transformers for Data-Driven Modeling of Low-Dimensional Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose the time-delayed transformer (TD-TF), a simplified transformer architecture for data-driven modeling of unsteady spatio-temporal dynamics. TD-TF bridges linear operator-based methods and deep sequence models by showing that a single-layer, single-head transformer can be interpreted as a nonlinear generalization of time-delayed dynamic mode decomposition (TD-DMD). The architecture is deliberately minimal, consisting of one self-attention layer with a single query per prediction and one feedforward layer, resulting in linear computational complexity in sequence length and a small parameter count. Numerical experiments demonstrate that TD-TF matches the performance of strong linear baselines on near-linear systems, while significantly outperforming them in nonlinear and chaotic regimes, where it accurately captures long-term dynamics. Validation studies on synthetic signals, unsteady aerodynamics, the Lorenz '63 system, and a reaction-diffusion model show that TD-TF preserves the interpretability and efficiency of linear models while providing substantially enhanced expressive power for complex dynamics.

papers.name: Strong Approximation for the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere
papers.abstract: We study the orbits of solutions to the Markoff-type equation $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + AX + BY + CZ + D$$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ for fixed integers $A,B,C,D$ under the group $Γ$ generated by \[\begin{split}&V_1: (x, y, z)\mapsto (A + yz - x, y, z),\\ &V_2: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, B + xz - y, z),\text{ and}\\ &V_3: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, y, C + xy - z).\end{split}\] This equation defines the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere, with $Γ$ arising from the Pure Mapping Class Group. Outside an explicit degeneracy locus, $Γ$ acts transitively on almost all solutions for a density-one set of primes independent of the parameters; the others split into small orbits reflecting finite orbits over $\mathbb{C}$. For ``degenerate'' parameters, we show there are two large orbits (most cases) or four (the rest, excluding $(0, 0, 0, 4)$) for the same primes. These results strengthen for two subfamilies. The first, $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + k,\,\,\,k\neq 4,$$ arises in the combinatorial group theory of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. Combined with Chen's work, $Γ$ acts transitively for all large primes, uniformly in $k$, so the $Q$-classification conjecture of McCullough and Wanderley holds over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for $p$ large. By Martin's work, so do their Classification and $T$-Classification Conjectures. The second, $$x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + a_1x_2x_3 + a_2x_1x_3 + a_3x_1x_2 = (3+a_1+a_2+a_3)x_1x_2x_3,$$ arises from generalized cluster algebras. Our degeneracy notion specializes to that of de Courcy-Ireland, Litman, and Mizuno, whose results similarly imply our orbit count (1, 2, or 4) for all large primes for all nondegenerate and some degenerate surfaces in that family.ds for all sufficiently large primes.

papers.name: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: Hausdorff dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
papers.abstract: We study the classical limiting laws of $\varphi(n)/n$ and $σ(n)/n$ over integers and shifted primes $p-1$. Let $μ_G$ denote the shifted-prime totient law and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. The law $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero, while every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-measure has packing dimension one. All four ratio laws and their logarithmic images have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions satisfying $0.550<\underline{d}_1\le\overline{d}_1<0.571$. The law $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both $μ_G$ and $μ_f$ have quantitative Fourier decay. For $μ_f$, we obtain sharp concentration asymptotics and localize maximizing intervals. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a random Euler product with an independent uniform phase. For a uniform square matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the probability of a primitive-root determinant tends, as the matrix size grows, to $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Over primes, $c(p)$ has limiting law $μ_G$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ over primes $p\le x$ converge to their common progression law with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. We also obtain transport estimates in growing progressions. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for every $A>0$, disproving the Erdős--Kátai singularity conjecture for $A>2$. Applications include extremal determinant bounds and certified prime selection without complete factorization of $p-1$. These results are unconditional; further quantitative refinements assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions.

papers.name: Jordan types for pairs of commuting nilpotent matrices: A survey
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to survey results on Jordan types for pairs of nilpotent commuting matrices. We also review recent proof of the Box Conjecture on Jordan types that have equal dense orbit in the nilpotent commutator.

papers.name: Bidirectional Random Projections
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes bidirectional random projections for ordinary least squares (OLS) regression under the fixed design setting. Let $(X, Y) \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a sample and $W \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n}$, $R \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p_1}$ be two random projections. We develop an expected excess loss bound for the OLS estimator built on $(WXR, WY)$, extending an established bound for the OLS estimator built on $(XR, Y)$. Our analysis shows that our bound is larger and the gap between the two bounds decays at a rate of approximately $O(1/n_1)$. These findings are confirmed by numerical results.

papers.name: On concatenation of matrices for reversible linear codes over a finite commutative ring and applications to DNA codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a generalized framework for constructing reversible linear, reversible self dual and reversible DNA codes using a matrix-theoretic approach based on involutory matrices. The proposed concatenation scheme gives a large class of generator matrices and yields codes with good parameters. The construction is carried out at the level of linear codes and then extended to DNA codes. Using a matrix product approach, we provide a unified method for analysis and proof. Further, we resolve an open problem raised by Oztas et.al. and also we correct and improve some results of them.

papers.name: Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension
papers.abstract: Consider the following plaquette model from statistical physics: a lamp lies at every vertex of the triangular lattice and a switch lies at every even vertex of the (bipartite) dual hexagonal lattice. Each switch toggles the three lamps on its face. The energy of a configuration is the number of ON lamps. For the Glauber dynamics associated with the Gibbs measure defined by this Hamiltonian at any inverse temperature $β>0$, we show that, in any dimension $d\ge 2$, the infinite volume relaxation time satisfies \[e^{β^2/C}/C \le T_{\mathrm{rel}}\le Ce^{e^{Cβ}}\] for some $C>0$. Our result entails that the Gibbs measure is unique. The $e^{β^2}$ scaling was conjectured by Garrahan and Newman in 2000 and matches the behaviour of supercritical rooted kinetically constrained models such as the East model, thus recovering fragile glass phenomenology in the absence of kinetic constraints. More precisely, we show that, on a torus of side length $2^k$, when $β\to\infty$ and $k/β\to0$, we have $T_{\mathrm{rel}}=e^{2βk(1+o(1))}$, confirming a prediction of Newman and Moore. Quite surprisingly, however, we also prove that, on non-periodic finite domains of size $n\le e^{β/C}$ for large $C>0$, we have the much larger asymptotics $\ln T_{\mathrm{rel}}=βn^{Θ(1)}$. The main ingredients of the proofs are new results in extremal and enumerative combinatorics and rely on renormalisation ideas for the dynamics and its groundstates also known as the Ledrappier subshift. Our combinatorial results also have consequences in geometric group theory (more precisely to the complexity of the word problem for the Baumslag finitely presented group), ergodic theory and linear coding theory.

papers.name: Consecutive integers free of certain prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $n_k$ denote the least integer $n>2k$ such that $(n-k)(n-k+1)\cdots(n-1)$ is not divisible by any prime in the interval $(k,2k)$. Confirming a conjecture of Erdős, we prove that, for all sufficiently large $k$, $$ n_k > e^{\frac{\log^2 k}{20 \log \log k}}. $$

papers.name: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For a central division $F$-algebras $L$ of a fixed degree $n$ we identify the double quotients of the homogeneous spaces $L_E^\times/L^\times$ with a topological space $Ξ_E$ which does not depend on a choice of $L$ , define a convolution products $\ast _L$ on the space ${\mathcal M} _E$ compactly supported measures on $Ξ_E$ and conjecture that the product $\ast _L$ on $Ξ_E$ does not depend on a choice of $L$.

papers.name: Characterization of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule and lattice points in flagged hive polytopes
papers.abstract: We have previously, for a given positive integer $n$, explicitly characterized by certain linear inequalities the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux of shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ produced by $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson (LR) rule. We now extend that characterization for lower shape lengths. Then using the composition of promotion operators defining the Naito-Suzuki-Watanabe bijection between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux, we also explicitly characterize by certain linear inequalities the corresponding $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux when the shape length is $2n$ or $2n-1$. In addition, when the given $n$ is $3$ or $ 4$ the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and the $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux are characterized by linear inequalities for lower shape lengths. Since recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule are in natural bijection with Littlewood-Richardson-Sundaram (LRS) tableaux, we relate our results on the inverse quantum LR rule with other two bijections for the Naito-Sagaki conjecture and establish bijections between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux, $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux and the lattice points in a (disjoint) union of flagged hive polytopes.

papers.name: Spectral Geroch conjecture and noncompact area enlargeable summands
papers.abstract: We study complete metrics on area enlargeable manifolds through the spectral constant $Λ_γ(g)$, the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient of $-Δ+γ\mathrm{scal}_g$ over compactly supported functions. We prove that every complete metric on an area enlargeable $m$-manifold, $m\ge2$, satisfies $Λ_γ(g)\le0$ for all $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. For an area enlargeable manifold $M_1$ and an oriented manifold $M_2$ of the same dimension, we prove that $M_1\#M_2$ is area enlargeable if and only if $M_2$ admits a spin covering. Both summands may be noncompact. Consequently, if the universal covering of $M_2$ is spin, then $M_1\#M_2$ carries neither a complete metric of positive scalar curvature nor a complete metric with positive $γ$-spectral constant for $γ>(m-1)/(4m)$. The threshold $(m-1)/(4m)$ is optimal. At the endpoint, the obstruction holds for metrics whose scalar curvature is bounded from below, but explicit complete warped metrics on $\mathbf{T}^{m-1}\times\mathbf{R}$ show that it fails in general. We also prove that the locally constant and the classical formulations of area enlargeability coincide in dimensions at least two.

papers.name: Homology of non-matching complexes under edge additions and applications to their Stanley-Reisner ideals
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph $G$ and an integer $t\geq 2$, we study the $t$-non-matching complex $\NM_t(G)$ and its Stanley-Reisner ideal. We prove that, if adding an edge $e$ to $G$ preserves bipartiteness, the inclusion $\NM_t(G)\hookrightarrow\NM_t(G+e)$ induces an injection on reduced homology in degree $2t-3$. If $G$ contains a cycle of length at least $2t$, then $\NM_t(G)$ has Leray number $2t-2$, and its Stanley-Reisner ideal has regularity $2t-1$. We also obtain explicit lower bounds for certain graded Betti numbers and the projective dimension of this ideal. If $G$ contains a $2t$-cycle, we determine the maximal shifts of this ideal through homological degree $|E(G)|-2t+1$. For the complete bipartite graph $G=K_{r, s}$ with $2\leq t\leq r\leq s$, we determine the depth, projective dimension, all maximal shifts, and the unique extremal Betti number of the associated ideal, thereby settling a conjecture on facet ideals of chessboard complexes.

papers.name: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

papers.name: Inverse theorems and non-arithmetic critical pairs for restricted sumsets in $\mathbb{Z}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $A,B\subset\mathbb{Z}_p$ be nonempty with $|A|\neq|B|$, and let $A\rplus B$ be the set of sums $a+b$ with $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and $a\neq b$. Alon, Nathanson and Ruzsa proved $|A\rplus B|\ge\min\{p,|A|+|B|-2\}$. Liu and Qian conjectured that when $|A|+|B|\le p$ equality forces $A$ and $B$ to be arithmetic progressions with a common difference, with $B$ the first or the last $|B|$ terms of $A$. We refute the conjecture. For every prime $p\ge11$ there is a critical pair with $|A|+|B|=p$, $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ and neither set an arithmetic progression, and for $p=13$ one with $|A|+|B|=p-2$. These pairs satisfy $|A|+2|B|\ge p+2$, and the inequality $|A+B|\le|A\rplus B|+|A\cap B|$ shows that no counterexample can do better. We conjecture that every critical pair with $|A|+2|B|\le p+1$ is arithmetic, and prove this when $|A+B|=|A|+|B|-1$. In the conjectured range the statement is equivalent to the minimality of the ordinary sumset, to a defect of one element, and to the emptiness of the band $|A|+|B|\le|A+B|\le p-1$. We also describe all critical pairs with $A+B=\mathbb{Z}_p$ at $p=|A|+2|B|-2$, and prove that every critical pair satisfies $|A\cap(A+t)|\ge|A|-|B|$ for $t\in B-B$ and that one with a uniquely represented restricted sum is arithmetic whenever all critical pairs with a smaller second set are.

papers.name: A General Inequality for Walks in Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and $w_k(G)$ denote the number of walks in $G$ of length $k$. For sequences $a_1, \cdots, a_n$ and $b_1, \cdots, b_n$ of non-negative integers such that $a_1 + \cdots + a_n = b_1 + \cdots + b_n$, we determine a simple necessary and sufficient condition on $a_1, \cdots, a_n, b_1, \cdots, b_n$ for the inequality \[ w_{a_1}(G) \cdots w_{a_n}(G) \geq w_{b_1}(G) \cdots w_{b_n}(G) \] to hold for any graph $G$.

papers.name: On intersection forms of spin $4$-manifolds with AR homology sphere boundary
papers.abstract: In this paper, building on the work of Dai--Sasahira--Stoffregen, we derive constraints on the intersection forms of smooth, compact, indefinite, spin $4$-manifolds bounded by almost-rational plumbed homology spheres (AR homology spheres) using two methods. First, we use the constraints on the existence of $\operatorname{Pin}(2)$-equivariant maps between representation spheres, established by Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu in their proof of the $10/8 + 4$-inequality. Second, we compute Lin's $κo$-invariant for AR homology spheres. Combined with Lin's version of the relative $10/8$-inequality, this computation yields constraints different from those based on Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu. As applications, we give an alternative proof of the non-sliceness of the $(2n, 1)$-cables of the figure-eight knot for even $n$---a result originally proved by Kang, Park, and Taniguchi via real Seiberg--Witten theory---by showing within ordinary Seiberg--Witten theory that certain cyclic branched covers of them are nontrivial in the homology cobordism group. We also obtain new lower bounds on the minimal genus of surfaces in various $4$-manifolds bounded by knots whose double branched covers are AR homology spheres. Moreover, we provide an obstruction to smooth $4$-manifold decompositions related to the $11/8$-conjecture.

papers.name: Determining $W^{1,n}$ conductivities for Calderón's problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: We establish a global uniqueness result at the critical Sobolev regularity for the isotropic Calderón problem in all dimensions $n \ge 4$. More precisely, for every $n \ge 4$ and every bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, any real-valued, uniformly elliptic scalar conductivity $γ\in W^{1,n}(Ω)$ is uniquely determined by its full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. Together with the known results for $n=2,3,4$ in the literature, this settles a long-standing open problem in the field while providing a unified proof for all dimensions $n \ge 4$. To prove uniqueness at this endpoint, we develop an averaged trace norm method, which combines complex geometrical optics with trace-norm estimates averaged over directions.

papers.name: A Dubnov-Ivanov-Nagata-Higman Theorem for NIP nilrings
papers.abstract: We prove that NIP nilrings of bounded nilexponent are nilpotent. We also deduce that NIP $ω$-categorical $n$-Engel Lie algebras of characteristic $p>n$ are nilpotent, yielding a case of the Lie algebra analogous of Wilson conjecture for $ω$-categorical groups.

papers.name: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity-free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by a $G$-stable symplectic lattice. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Q_p)$, we prove, under suitable assumptions, the existence of certain paths in $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ and show that $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.

papers.name: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
papers.abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a new relative BFK type gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles and discuss some extremal properties.

papers.name: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions associated with polynomial sequences satisfying a first-order differential recurrence. As applications, we prove weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials, several families of Eulerian polynomials, the Bell polynomials, and the reflected generalized Laguerre polynomials. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai concerning the Bell and Laguerre polynomials.

papers.name: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
papers.abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

papers.name: The Dimension Conjecture for Hypersurfaces Is True
papers.abstract: The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for arbitrary real-analytic hypersurfaces. More precisely, for $N\ge2$ the dimension of the Lie algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ of the indicated class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This is exactly the dimension of the corresponding algebra for any Levi-nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric. For a finitely nondegenerate hypersurface with constant positive Levi rank $r$ satisfying $0<r<N-1$, the sharper bound $N^2+r+1=N^2+N-m$ is obtained, where $m=N-1-r$. We also establish the sharper bound $N^2+N-1$ for the automorphism algebra of a nonspherical holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface; consequently, dimensions $N^2+N,...,N^2+2N-1$ cannot occur (a dimension gap).

papers.name: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
papers.abstract: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

papers.name: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
papers.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

papers.name: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$.
