They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for meshes with at least 512 elements and the failure of both bounds have proofs checked by Lean 4. The only premise is the mesh-uniform Crandall-Pazy estimate of the W-scheme (arXiv:2610.39269). Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

papers.name: Perdomo's index conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: Let $x:M^n\to\sphere^{n+1}(1)$, $n\ge2$, be a full minimal immersion of a closed, connected, oriented manifold. We prove that its Morse index is at least $n+3$, with equality precisely for the standard Clifford embeddings. For a non-Clifford image, the constant function and the position and normal coordinates span a space containing an $(n+4)$-dimensional subspace on which the Jacobi quadratic form is negative definite. Thus we resolve Perdomo's index conjecture.

papers.name: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in short intervals
papers.abstract: Let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from a real number $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $α$ be any irrational number and $β_0$ any real number. We prove that there exist infinitely many $X$ such that for $Y=X^γ/2$ with $7/12<γ\le 1$ and $0<θ<\min \{(12γ-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there is a prime $p$ satisfying $$ \|αp+β_0\|<X^{-θ},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. In particular, if $α$ has a continued fraction expansion with bounded partial quotients, then this asymptotic holds for all sufficiently large $X$. Our result improves upon a previous result of Baier and Roy by extending the admissible range of the short interval parameter from $2/3<γ\le 1$ to $7/12<γ\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals, and also improves the exponent $θ$ for $2/3\leγ\le3/4$. The improvement is obtained by adapting a recent result of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł on exponential sums over primes.

papers.name: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$Ω$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.

papers.name: Log-concavity of rank and crank statistics for integer partitions
papers.abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang [Adv. Math. 2021] conjectured that $M(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$, and that $N(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge73$ and $|m|\le n-73$. In this paper, we prove these two conjectures.

papers.name: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.name: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $ξ$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $ζ$ of $p$ such that $ |ξ-ζ|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.The Lean 4 formalization of the main results are also provided.

papers.name: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
papers.abstract: We study the structural dimension of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

papers.name: Global Hyperbolicity Criterion for Regular Sub-Lorentzian Manifolds
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global hyperbolicity of regular sub-Lorentzian manifolds. We establish a criterion for global hyperbolicity on complete Riemannian manifolds, formulated in terms of a smooth time function and an admissible growth function. The proof relies on the theory of differential inclusions. The proposed condition relaxes the classical requirements on the differential of the time function. The effectiveness of the obtained criterion is illustrated on classical nonholonomic structures: the Grushin space, the Heisenberg group, and step-2 Carnot groups, for which we find explicit asymptotic bounds on the expansion rate of causal cones that guarantee the preservation of global hyperbolicity.

papers.name: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link which is not Lorenz, thereby disproving the Birman--Kofman conjecture that every horseshoe link is a Lorenz link. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

papers.name: Maximality of the Došen-Petrić Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.name: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

papers.name: Discontinuity-Aware Solvers for Vapor-Compression Cycles
papers.abstract: Physics-based models of vapor-compression cycles are often formulated as large, stiff DAE systems with derivative discontinuities introduced at the points of phase change. We use an implementation of a discontinuity-aware ODE and DAE solver scheme that uses domain-specific, user-declared information to compute appropriate time steps for more efficient integration. This scheme is made open-source within Julia's DifferentialEquations package. We demonstrate how discontinuity information can be specified symbolically in a declarative modeling language such as Dyad and passed to the solver to address the numerical challenges posed. We apply this discontinuity-aware technique to two applications: first, a scalar ODE with two discontinuities, and then a model of a full vapor-compression cycle. The discontinuity-aware solver yields significantly fewer step rejections and improved solver times, particularly with the Rodas5P solver at loose tolerances, as compared to standard error control, suggesting that exposing physical discontinuity information from equation-oriented models to adaptive solvers can improve practical simulation performance without requiring reassembly of the model.

papers.name: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

papers.name: Abelian varieties with homotheties
papers.abstract: In 1980, Bogomolov proved that the $\ell$-adic Galois image of an Abelian variety over a number field contains an open subgroup of the homotheties. In 1986, Serre refined that result, showing that the homotheties coming from the Galois side were uniformly bounded in $\ell$ inside the homotheties of the codomain of the representation. In a 2007 paper, Zarhin shows that Bogomolov's conclusion can fail in non-trivial cases for global function fields. We prove a suitable analogue of Serre's results over finitely generated fields of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we prove a new case of the 1978 conjecture by Geyer and Jarden.

papers.name: A Burns-Krantz theorem on convex domains
papers.abstract: We prove two boundary rigidity theorems for holomorphic self-maps of bounded convex domains. Let $Ω\subset\C^n$, $n\geq1$, and suppose that $\partialΩ$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $p\in\partialΩ$ for some $0<α\leq1$. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ satisfies $f(z)=z+o(|z-p|^3)$ as $z\to p$ in one fixed non-tangential approach region at $p$, then $f=\id_Ω$. We also prove a rigidity theorem for bounded convex domains $Ω$ without assuming boundary smoothness. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ of $Ω$ satisfies $f(z)-z=O(|z-p|^m)$ as $z\to p\in\partialΩ$ for some $m>1+2π/θ_p$, where $θ_p$ is the supremum of sector angles in the open tangent cone at $p$, taken over complex lines through its vertex, then $f=\id_Ω$, which proves a conjecture of Zimmer.

papers.name: On (Pathwidth, Clique)-boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove that every $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class of graphs has bounded tree-independence number, answering a question of Bešter Štorgel, Dallard, Lozin, Milanič, and Zamaraev. We deduce this from a bound on the tree-independence number of graphs with neither $\B_ρ$ nor $K_{σ,σ}$ as an induced minor, where $\B_ρ$ is the complete binary tree of height $ρ$ and the bound depends only on $ρ$ and $σ$. We then obtain an asymptotically sharp bound on the path-independence number of $n$-vertex graphs in any $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class. The lower-bound examples also give counterexamples to a conjecture of Hickingbotham and Joret. We further prove that, for every forest $F$ and every $\ell\in\N$, there is a constant $k=k(F,\ell)\in\N$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced theta or $\ell$-long prism and no induced subgraph isomorphic to $F$ satisfies tree-independence number at most $k$. This proves a strengthened form of a conjecture of Chudnovsky, Hajebi, and Trotignon. Finally, for every integer $s\ge2$, we characterize the forests $F$ for which excluding $F$ as an induced minor and $K_{s,s}$ as an induced subgraph bounds tree-independence number. This extends the characterization of Bonnet, Duhamel, and Hickingbotham, who considered bounded pathwidth with $K_{s,s}$ excluded as a subgraph.

papers.name: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
papers.abstract: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

papers.name: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
papers.abstract: Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value. For matrices of odd order, the sharp cardinality bound was already established by Delsarte and Goethals (1975). In this paper, we prove the Cooperstein conjecture for matrices of even order and, more generally, we prove its additive analogue by determining, for all admissible parameters, the maximum size of an additive subgroup of alternating matrices in which every nonzero matrix has at least the prescribed rank. Our proof uses Pfaffian equations to characterize alternating matrices of rank below the prescribed minimum. We study the minimal graded free resolutions of the corresponding Pfaffian rings. The Cohen--Macaulay property and the $a$-invariant of each Pfaffian ring determine the largest shift in its resolution. We use trace functions on evaluation quotients to construct polynomial indicators for the matrices of small rank in an additive subgroup. The largest shift controls their degrees, yielding the upper bound by a counting argument. Finally, we give explicit trace constructions attaining the bound.

papers.name: Nonlinear syzygies in ordinary powers of chordal cover ideals
papers.abstract: We construct connected chordal graphs whose cover ideals have ordinary powers that are not componentwise linear over any field, disproving the Herzog--Hibi--Ohsugi conjecture.

papers.name: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
papers.abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we show $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjecture this for all prime powers.

papers.name: Exact and Approximate Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Multivariate Diffusions under High-Frequency Sampling
papers.abstract: We establish the asymptotic theory of the exact maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for discretely observed multivariate ergodic diffusions under high-frequency, long-span sampling, solving an open problem posed by \citet{YCW2019} and \citet{Li2013}. The drift may grow linearly, and the volatility is bounded away from zero and either bounded or proportional to $1+|x|$. When the sampling interval decays polynomially, the exact MLE is consistent, asymptotically normal and efficient, with rates $\sqrt{nΔ_n}$ for drift and $\sqrt n$ for diffusion parameters. Under an additional condition on ergodic averages, and when the time span $nΔ_n$ also grows polynomially, its moments converge as well. The proof never analyzes the exact likelihood directly: it shows that a closed-form density expansion of sufficiently high order is uniformly accurate in relative terms at every observed transition, so that the two log-likelihoods differ by $o_P(1)$ uniformly in the parameter. The same argument yields accuracy conditions under which an approximate likelihood is asymptotically equivalent to the exact one; in particular, the approximate MLE of Yang, Chen and Wan converges to the true parameter. For the delta-expansion estimator of fixed order $K\ge1$, we derive the leading bias explicitly. It shows that $nΔ_n^{K+1}\to0$ cannot be weakened when the bias constant is nonzero, and that the bias falls on the drift parameters for even $K$ and on the diffusion parameters for odd $K$. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the predicted biases.

papers.name: The minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for some k
papers.abstract: A graph on at least 2k+2 vertices is k-extendable if every matching of size k extends to a perfect matching, and it is minimally k-extendable if it is k-extendable but deleting any edge is not. Plummer proved that every k-extendable graph is (k+1)-connected. So its minimum degree is at least k+1. Lou and Yu conjectured that a minimally k-extendable graph on at most 4k vertices has minimum degree in {k+1,2k,2k+1}; the case k=1 and the claw-free case of k=2 have been settled previously. We determine the minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for k=2 and k=3, thereby settling the Lou--Yu conjecture for these two values. For k=2 the minimum degree is in {3,4,5}. For k=3 it is in {4,7} at orders 8 and 10, and in {4,6,7} at order 12. The proofs pass to the complement graph and combine Tutte's perfect matching theorem with a classification of four-vertex and six-vertex obstructions. All predicted values are realized by explicit constructions.

papers.name: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
papers.abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

papers.name: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
papers.abstract: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$. We prove that $a_k(n)\ge0$ for all $k,n\ge0$, thereby resolving a conjecture on signed odd-multiplicity partitions. Our proof combines a positive theta--MacMahon factorization for the generating functions restricted to odd part sizes with a dyadic product decomposition that extends positivity to arbitrary part sizes. Moreover, we establish strict positivity $a_k(n)>0$ for every $k\ge2$ and $n\ge\binom{k+1}{2}$.

papers.name: Global rigidity and the Hessian energy identity for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
papers.abstract: We prove that every entire classical stable solution of the one-phase Bernoulli problem in dimension five or six is one-dimensional. In dimensions three through six, we establish an exact interior identity for the scale-invariant Hessian energy of sequences with bounded Morse index. Hence, the global stability conjecture is solved.

papers.name: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$). We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit and Langlands correspondence is not needed for its description (it is a principle ideal, where the generator is given by some version of the discriminant function). We also prove our general conjecture for $G=\mathrm{SL}(2)$.

papers.name: An extremal question of Erdős et al. on cycles
papers.abstract: This paper addresses an extremal problem on long cycles proposed by Erdős, Faudree, Schelp and Simonovits in 1989. Let \(2\le k\le d<n\) be positive integers. For an n-vertex simple graph G, let \(θ_+^G\) count vertices of degree at least d, and \(C_{\ge k+1}\) denote a cycle of length at least \(k+1\). The original conjecture claimed that G contains a \(C_{\ge k+1}\) whenever \(θ_+^G \ge \lfloor k/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/d \rfloor+2\). Li, Ma and Ning disproved it with infinite counterexamples and gave linear lower bounds. Gan, Yi and Jiang later obtained piecewise sufficient conditions depending on the parity of k, whose bounds are sharp only when \(k=d\) and loose for \(k\ne d\). We derive a new sufficient condition for \(C_{\ge k+1}\). For odd \(k=d\), we use Woodall's sharp bound \(θ_+^G \ge k(n-2)/(2(k-1))+1\). For all other admissible parameters, our threshold is unified and independent of the parity of k: \(θ_+^G \ge \lfloor k/2 \rfloor (n-1)/d + (n-d-1)\lfloor k/2 \rfloor/(d(d-\lfloor k/2 \rfloor))+1\). We construct \(C_{\ge k+1}\)-free graphs to prove tightness for all admissible k. This resolves this long-standing Erdős-type extremal problem concerning high-degree vertices and long cycles.

papers.name: Moser--Trudinger inequalities and the complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation
papers.abstract: We study sharp Moser--Trudinger inequalities for the complex Monge--Ampère energy. On the unit ball, we determine the optimal energy coefficient and additive constant in the logarithmic Moser--Trudinger inequality. We deduce subcritical Moser--Trudinger inequalities in exponential form with explicit bounds proportional to $\varepsilon^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the relative distance to the critical coefficient. The proof establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness for the associated mean field equation by showing that every smooth solution has constant boundary normal derivative. This gives existence and uniqueness precisely for total masses $0<Λ<[2π(n+1)]^n$, proving Berman--Berndtsson's conjecture. We also establish smoothness of bounded pluripotential and finite-energy solutions. Domain monotonicity transfers the exponential estimates and the optimal logarithmic energy coefficient to bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains.

papers.name: Equivalence of Small and Large Quasi-kernels
papers.abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set which can reach every vertex of $D$ by a directed path of length at most 2. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex source-free digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q|\le n/2$, and the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]|\ge n/2$. Our main result shows for any $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$ an equivalence between the following two statements: \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex source-free digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |Q|\le n-Ω(n^β).\] \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |N^+[Q]|\ge Ω(n^{2-\frac{1}β}).\] That is, any sublinear bound for one problem is equivalent to a corresponding sublinear bound for the other. This combined with previous work establishing an equivalence for linear bounds shows that the two problems are largely equivalent to each other. We additionally give a slight refinement to the recent breakthrough of Rutschmann for these problems which, together with the result above, gives the best known bounds of $n-Ω(n^{3/4})$ and $Ω(n^{2/3})$ for the Small and Large Quasi-kernel Conjectures, respectively. Our proofs are due to ChatGPT's Astra 6; the writing is all our own.

papers.name: Minimum outdegree forcing directed cycles
papers.abstract: The Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture, one of the best known open problems on oriented graphs, asserts that every oriented graph on $n$ vertices with minimum outdegree at least $n/\ell$ contains a directed cycle of length at most $\ell$. Motivated by it, Kelly, Kühn and Osthus asked for the minimum degree condition that forces a directed cycle of length exactly $\ell$. The semidegree version of this problem was recently solved, but the methods used there rely on bounding the directed diameter, which requires control over the indegrees. In the setting of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture, where only the outdegrees are bounded, the answer was known only for $\ell$ not divisible by $3$. We determine the optimal minimum outdegree forcing a directed cycle of length $\ell$ for every sufficiently large $\ell$ and $n$. This establishes the outdegree version of the Kelly-Kühn-Osthus conjecture for all large $\ell$, up to a small correction of the additive term, which in general cannot be avoided.

papers.name: On Ext-groups between Arthur-type modules of the graded Hecke algebras of type A
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb H_n$ be the graded Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. This article establishes a formula for Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and a $W$-type $\mathbb H_n$-module in terms of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain an explicit and efficient method to compute Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and an Arthur-type module of $\mathbb H_n$. In particular, this proves new instances of a conjecture of Chan and Prasad on Ext non-vanishing between Arthur-type representations. We also discuss some other non-Ext vanishing results for calibrated modules.

papers.name: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
papers.abstract: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A.Hanlon, J.Hicks, and O.Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

papers.name: On Green's Conjecture for Curves on Anticanonical Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove Green's conjecture for smooth curves $C$ on rational surfaces $X$ such that $-K_X|_C$ is effective on $C$. In addition, on birationally ruled surfaces $X$ of irregularity $q \geq 1$ carrying an effective anticanonical divisor, we show that Green's conjecture holds for all smooth curves $C$ on $X$ covering the base curve with degree at least $2$, provided the latter has only finitely many gonal pencils or the gonality of $C$ is special with respect to the ruling.

papers.name: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
papers.abstract: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.

papers.name: Higher-Derivative Conjectures of Sendov
papers.abstract: We prove Conjectures~3 and~8 of Sendov's 2002 survey and deduce Conjecture~9. More precisely, let $p$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. For every integer $s$ with $1\le s<n$, we prove that each zero of $p$ lies within distance $2s/(s+1)$ of a zero of $p^{(s)}$. For quartics, we obtain the sharp bound $2/\sqrt3$ for the second derivative and determine all polynomials attaining it.

papers.name: First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons
papers.abstract: We develop a first order calculus based on the geometry of realised diameter graphs for perimeter maximisation among convex equilateral small polygons. Polygon side equalities and active diameter constraints define a linearised feasible cone and an associated equality space. We prove that an equilateral small polygon is a strict local maximiser of perimeter modulo Euclidean motions if a multiplier balance holds with strictly positive active diameter multipliers and the active equality space consists only of infinitesimal Euclidean motions. The proof uses a local Euclidean slice and a geometric limiting argument and requires neither independence of the active constraint gradients nor second order information. As an application, we combine our criterion with validated interval arithmetic to establish strict local maximality for Bingane and Audet's polygons $A_{16}$, $A_{32}$, $A_{64}$ and for reconstructions of their polygons $Z_{32}$ and $Z_{64}$. For each $n\in\{32,64\}$, the perimeter of $Z_n$ is strictly larger than that of $A_n$. Thus, strict local maximisers with different perimeters coexist in the space of convex equilateral small polygons with the same number of sides.

papers.name: Well-posedness of compressible $2D$ nonlinear transport equations and quasiconformal maps
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of solutions to a class of nonlinear transport equations in the plane, for which the velocity field is obtained as the convolution of the classical Cauchy kernel with the unknown. Even though the initial datum is bounded and compactly supported, the velocity field may have unbounded divergence. The proof relies on the theory of quasiconformal mappings.

papers.name: Divisible design graphs from a construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a new construction of divisible design graphs with new parameters, obtained by plugging a difference set into a known construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs of diameter 3 that is based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups.

papers.name: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

papers.name: The Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem
papers.abstract: In a previous paper, the authors established the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem, which generalizes the Stone-von Neumann Theorem in quantum mechanics and yields a classification of all unitary Heisenberg representations of an abelian elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system up to unitary equivalence. In this sequel to that paper, we establish an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem in the setting of real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical systems. Firstly, we generalize Stone's Theorem to secure a one-to-one correspondence between the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and the regular self-adjoint densely defined operators on a Hilbert $ C^{\ast} $-module. Secondly, we define the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations and the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system. Thirdly, we construct a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary Heisenberg representation and the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, providing a rigorous two-way passage--which we call ``Heisenberg differentiability-integrability''--between the global unitary formulation of Heisenberg covariance and its infinitesimal formulation in terms of regular self-adjoint densely defined operators. This allows us to prove the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: For a real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation is a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation. Lastly, we obtain explicit descriptions of the position and momentum operators for a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system and construct a natural common invariant core of analytic vectors for them. All requisite technical domain and integrability issues are fully accounted for.

papers.name: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampère equations in big classes
papers.abstract: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampère equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact Kähler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,α}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.

papers.name: Spectral Classification of Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
papers.abstract: We study the unscaled empirical singular spectra of deterministic skew Hilbert--Schmidt kernels evaluated on independent isotropic rows satisfying a uniform quadratic-form variance bound. For arbitrary varying kernels at spatial dimension $d$, tightness and collapse to zero are characterized by boundedness and vanishing, respectively, of the rescaled quadratic energy remaining after deletion of $\lfloor\varepsilon d\rfloor$ leading skew pairs, for every $\varepsilon>0$. A regularized positive-covariance detector proves the necessary direction without a spectral envelope and retains diffuse energy across arbitrarily many small modes. On this exact tightness class, a weighted deterministic source characterizes all probability limits of the empirical spectra through the classical canonical parametrization of symmetric freely infinitely divisible laws. For a fixed kernel, convergence of one bounded resolvent response to a positive deterministic limit, convergence of one normalized logarithmic determinant, and full empirical spectral convergence are each equivalent to a critical Weyl law; the limit is necessarily a possibly degenerate half-Cauchy law. Finally, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for polygonal Brownian Lévy-area spectra to recover the continuous-time bulk under arbitrary deterministic time partitions, even when the normalized mean-square matrix error diverges.

papers.name: New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study extremal densities of measurable subsets of metric spaces avoiding prescribed finite geometric configurations. We prove two new upper bounds for three-point avoidance problems: a measurable subset of $S^2$ containing no orthonormal basis has normalized spherical measure at most $7/11$, and a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing no unit equilateral triangle has upper Banach density at most $9/16$. The first bound appears to be the first improvement over the trivial averaging bound for this problem, while the second improves the previously best known upper bound. The proofs are applications of the geometric fractional chromatic number method introduced by Ambrus et al. For this purpose, we formulate the method in a framework that applies both to compact homogeneous spaces and to Euclidean spaces with upper Banach density.

papers.name: Sparse optimal control for a class of infinite-dimensional bilinear systems: optimality conditions and uniqueness
papers.abstract: We study optimal control of an evolution equation in which a scalar control multiplies a bounded operator acting on the state, with free dynamics given by a $C_0$-semigroup. The cost combines tracking terms, a quadratic control cost and an $L^1$ term promoting sparsity in time. We prove existence, derive optimality conditions, and show that optimal controls are thresholded functions of a switching function whose derivative is governed by the commutator of the drift and control operators. Consequently, commuting problems with a terminal cost admit no temporally sparse controls. The $L^1$ term also matters for uniqueness: two distinct controls satisfying the optimality conditions differ on a set of measure bounded from below, contained in the union of their supports, which yields, for the first time, uniqueness for every horizon in stable problems steered to zero. Second-order sufficient conditions and experiments on a bilinear heat equation complete the study.

papers.name: An algorithm for solving structured problems involving $L$-infimal convolutions
papers.abstract: We develop an operator-splitting framework for solving structured minimization problems involving linear compositions of $L$-infimal convolutions. We introduce a primal-dual shadow Douglas-Rachford splitting method and establish its convergence. As a result, we derive a fully primal-dual splitting algorithm for the class of the aforementioned minimization problems.

papers.name: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
papers.abstract: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imathπ/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quantum Riemannian geometry, we construct a natural Einstein--Hilbert action and hence new quantum gravity models on $A_3,D_4,\widetilde D_4,\widetilde D_5,\widetilde D_6,\widetilde E_6$ in a functional integral approach, other than the 4-star $\widetilde D_4$ which we revisit.

papers.name: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.

papers.name: Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable. Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest. We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an explicit family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of sub-exponential size. This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.

papers.name: Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability
papers.abstract: Min-entropy plays a fundamental role in assessing the unpredictability of randomness sources. In particular, NIST SP 800-90B specifies min-entropy estimation as a key procedure for entropy sources used in cryptographic random bit generators, illustrating the practical importance of reliable min-entropy estimation. In this paper, we settle the sample complexity of min-entropy estimation with high probability in both the classical and quantum cases. Specifically, for min-entropy estimation with additive error $\varepsilon$ and probability at least $1-δ$, the sample complexity is $Θ(d\log(d/δ)/\varepsilon^2)$ for classical distributions on $d$ symbols and $Θ((d^2+d\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ for quantum states on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. Our results admit short and simple proofs.

papers.name: Tropicalization and slow manifolds: A case study of the Michaelis--Menten reaction
papers.abstract: We present a case study of a recently developed approach to multiple-scale systems based on exponential scaling and tropicalization (Kristiansen and Sarantaris, \emph{On a tropicalization of planar polynomial ODEs}). Parameters and variables are scaled exponentially with respect to a small parameter $ε$, so that orders of magnitude become a genuine non-smooth singular limit $ε\to 0$. Tropical geometry, via subdivisions of the Newton polygon, classifies the asymptotic regimes and locates the candidates for slow manifolds on all scales of the variables simultaneously. Here we combine this framework with blow-up and geometric singular perturbation theory. {In particular,} the non-smooth singular limit is resolved by spherical and cylindrical blow-ups, and degeneracies caused by exponentially small terms with flat contact are treated by adding the exponential quantities as new variables {(following Kristiansen, \emph{Blowup for flat slow manifolds})}. As the case study, we take the Michaelis--Menten reaction. The tropical classification yields three asymptotic regimes of parameters. In two of these, we find a sequence of blowups and desingularizations where the system has a {global} normally hyperbolic critical manifold on the blown up space. In the remaining case, we obtain a similar result, but only for a subcase. In particular, there is an asymptotic regime of parameters where there is no global slow manifold of the Michaelis--Menten reaction.

papers.name: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

papers.name: Inverse Boundary Value Problems for a Coupled Semilinear Klein-Gordon System
papers.abstract: This article addresses the coefficient identification inverse problem for a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with cubic nonlinearity. More precisely, we consider a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in a bounded cylinder contained in $\mathbb{R}^{1+\ell}$, where $ \ell\geq 2$, and establish the unique recovery of the time-independent coefficients appearing in both the zeroth-order perturbation and nonlinearity term from both full and partial boundary measurements of the solution. The unique recovery of zeroth-order coefficients is obtained via first-order linearization; however, the nonlinearity coefficients are recovered using the higher-order linearization. Finally using the unique continuation principle, we establish the unique identification of the coefficients from the partial boundary measurements of the solution.

papers.name: $p$-harmonic polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that every real polynomial $p$-harmonic function on $\Rn$ is affine when $n\ge3$ and $p\ge n-1/13$. The proof uses the Bernstein--Szegő inequality on great circles and a deficit estimate at the first Chebyshev node.

papers.name: $\ell^p$-Improving for Discrete Fractional Integrals and Averages on the Moment Curve
papers.abstract: We prove the $\ell^p$-improving estimates in the full range for discrete fractional integral operators on the moment curve (except at the endpoint) and discrete averages on the moment curve (with $N^ε$-losses). This follows via essentially sharp Diophantine solution counting estimates for inhomogeneous Vinogradov systems with an odd number of variables.

papers.name: General curves on smooth quadric hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp existence theorem for non-degenerate maps from a general curve to a smooth quadric hypersurface, deforming in a smooth family of expected dimension. Along the way, we prove that if a general curve in projective space lies on a quadric (as dictated by the Maximal Rank Conjecture, now a theorem of E. Larson), then a general such quadric is smooth.

papers.name: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. The bulk viscosity satisfies a logarithmic derivative bound and a growth condition on its primitive, including every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with a logarithmic gain larger than one half. Time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponential convergence to the nonconstant hydrostatic state are obtained. For strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential convergence to the hydrostatic state in higher Sobolev norms are proved. An initial vacuum point persists and causes exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.name: A Normal Form for Invertible Semilinear Maps and the Category of Isocrystals Over a Finite Field
papers.abstract: For a field $L$, and a finite order automorphism $σ$, we classify invertible $σ$-semilinear endomorphisms on finite-dimensional $L$-vector spaces up to equivalence. This is deduced as a consequence of a description, in terms of certain norm equations in finite extensions of $L$, of the semilinear Schur indices for the group $\mathbb{Z}$ acting on $L$ via $σ$. As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.

papers.name: Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure. We use this grading to show that Dehn twists give faithful braid group representations in the symplectic mapping class groups of Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds.

papers.name: Determining Compatible Groups in $Γ$-Zonal Labelings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a plane graph with vertex, edge, and region sets $V(G),$ $E(G),$ and $F(G)$ respectively, and let $Γ$ be a nontrivial abelian group with identity element $0$. A $Γ$-zonal labeling of a plane graph $G$ is a labeling $\ell: V(G)\rightarrow Γ\setminus\{0\}$ such that for every region $f\in F(G)$, the sum of labels on the boundary of $f$ is $0$ in $Γ$. We say a $Γ$-zonal labeling is generative if the labels used generate $Γ$, and strong if the additive order of each label matches the degree of the corresponding vertex. Given a graph $G$ or a family of graphs $\mathcal{G}$, we explore restrictions on the groups $Γ$ for which there can exist a $Γ$-zonal labeling. Here we specifically determine restrictions on compatible groups when $\mathcal{G}$ is the family of $2$-connected multigraphs or $2$-connected simple graphs. We also demonstrate how the Smith normal form decomposition of the face incidence matrix of a plane graph $G$ can help characterize the groups $Γ$ for which there exists a generative $Γ$-zonal labeling.

papers.name: A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds
papers.abstract: We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category. Along the way of defining the bordism-end, we show that the category of all smooth $d$-dimensional manifolds and embeddings is formally obtained from the analogous category of compact manifolds. Through the formalism of the bordism-end, it follows that a manifold is diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold if and only if its bordism-end is representable. Moreover, this formalism yields a fibre sequence relating the classifying spaces of the compactly supported diffeomorphism group of a manifold and its full diffeomorphism group, and a space of bordism-ends. Finally, we set up the pro-end functorially in embeddings, with target the cospan $\infty$-category of pro-spaces, and show that it factors through the bordism-end.

papers.name: Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.

papers.name: On the V-toothpick sequence
papers.abstract: We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.

papers.name: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification
papers.abstract: Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes. We first study linear diffusion, where node values evolve according to the graph Laplacian. The dominant network sparsification method, effective resistance sampling, preserves all Laplacian eigenvalues within a uniform multiplicative bound. We show that with a limited edge budget, this is dynamically inefficient: diffusion is dominated by the slowest-decaying modes, so enforcing a uniform guarantee spends edges on fast modes that barely affect long-term dynamics. Based on this observation, we derive Diffusion Spectral Error (DSE), which evaluates in closed form the typical error in trajectories between the original and sparsified graphs over random initial conditions. Minimizing this error, which naturally prioritizes slow modes, yields sparse networks explicitly designed to preserve dynamics. At the same sparsification levels, DSE sparsification often preserves diffusion dynamics with several-fold lower error than effective resistance sampling, and up to two orders of magnitude lower on strongly modular networks. Although derived in a linear context, we empirically find that DSE sparsification gives similar improvements in the Kuramoto model (a nonlinear system of coupled oscillators), where DSE sparsification approximately preserves the synchronization threshold and, at strong coupling, order-parameter trajectories.

papers.name: Cutoff on abelian groups
papers.abstract: We prove the long-predicted equivalence between the cutoff phenomenon and the product condition along any sequence of abelian random walks whose inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with the size of the group. Our result does not require reversibility, and comes with a sharp quantitative estimate on the mixing window. Moreover, we show that our sparsity restriction is optimal by constructing abelian Cayley graphs which satisfy the product condition but fail to exhibit cutoff, and whose degrees are arbitrarily close to being logarithmic in the volume.

papers.name: Second-class particle in ASEP. Rarefaction fan
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a second class particle in ASEP on the integer lattice. We prove a general formula for the distribution of its position at any fixed time for arbitrary initial conditions. As a first application, we obtain its limiting distribution for arbitrary initial conditions in the rarefaction fan case, generalizing the result of Cator--Pimentel from TASEP to ASEP.

papers.name: Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
papers.abstract: DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.

papers.name: Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders
papers.abstract: We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $β^{-αn}$ at order $n$, where $β>1$ and $0<α\le1$. We characterize their pointwise Hölder regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable. For beta-expansion cylinders, we compute the full multifractal spectrum whenever the remainders of the expansion of $1$ have a finite upper exponential decay rate. The functions are monofractal when this rate vanishes, as it does for Parry, Pisot and Salem bases. When it is positive, the spectrum is affine on a nondegenerate interval. The bases defined by $\sum_{k\ge0}β_\ell^{-\ell^k}=1$, for integers $\ell\ge2$, give explicit non-monofractal examples. We also prove that every function in the family is nowhere differentiable.

papers.name: Circular Vector Tomography with Partial Radial Data
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce and study several generalized circular Radon transforms acting on smooth vector fields compactly supported in a planar annulus, with centers restricted to the outer acquisition circle and truncated measurement radii. The operators of interest are the longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transforms and their weighted analogues. We characterize the kernels of the individual unweighted transforms. Then we establish the reconstruction of a vector field from the combined longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transform data. We further show that the pairs formed by each transform and its weighted analogue is not sufficient for the complete recovery of a vector field. However, we demonstrate that full reconstruction is possible with suitable additional data. Finally, we numerically implement and validate the derived inversion formulas.

papers.name: Non-homogeneous parabolic conormal boundary problem with singular-degenerate coefficients
papers.abstract: We study non-homogeneous conormal boundary value problems for a class of divergence-form parabolic equations whose volumetric heat-capacity coefficients belong to a Muckenhoupt class of weights. Consequently, the equations exhibit singular, degenerate, or simultaneously singular-degenerate behavior. Under smallness conditions on the partial mean oscillation of the diffusion coefficients and the weighted mean oscillation of the volumetric heat-capacity coefficient, we establish regularity estimates, existence, and uniqueness results in appropriate weighted Sobolev spaces. To obtain these results, we employ the level-set argument introduced by Caffarelli and Peral. We also establish weighted parabolic cylinders, weighted inequalities, and a weighted Aubin-Lions compactness theorem, which are essential tools in our analysis.

papers.name: Asymptotics of Gibbs Posterior Measures on Infinite-Dimensional Hypothesis Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove almost sure contraction rates and consistency for Gibbs posterior measures on arbitrary hypothesis spaces, in general infinite dimensional, under dependent data, nonadditive and time-dependent losses and learning rates, misspecified models, and unattainable minimisers of the limiting objective. In particular, we develop a novel proof approach in contraction rate theory by studying the asymptotics of Gibbs measures through Lorentz spaces, real interpolation theory, and Laplace transforms dispensing with testing or variational formulations which are unavailable in the considered generality. As a consequence we obtain almost sure contraction rates for dominated Bayes and fractional Bayes posterior measures in the same generality, extending existing theory on misspecified Bayesian inference. Furthermore, we demonstrate our theoretical results on novel applications to Gibbs posteriors for Dirichlet process priors with a nonadditive Wasserstein metric loss function under ergodic, non-Markovian observables.

papers.name: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$. To narrow this gap, we propose an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient (SVRG) method that significantly improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Furthermore, when the objective consists of a single function, the proposed method reduces to a novel deterministic first-order method for solving standard convex conic optimization. It achieves a significantly lower gradient evaluation complexity with respect to the objective function compared to existing methods, and can outperform them when computing constraint gradients and projections onto the associated cone is cheaper than evaluating the objective gradient. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

papers.name: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce relative Sidorenko and relative anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs, strengthening the corresponding well-studied notions for tournaments by allowing arbitrary host graphs. An orientation $\vec H$ of a graph $H$ is relatively Sidorenko if $\hom(\vec H,\vec G) \ge 2^{-e(H)}\hom(H,G)$ for every oriented graph $\vec G$ with underlying graph $G$, and relatively anti-Sidorenko if the reverse inequality holds. We provide a complete characterisation of the class of connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs, and exhibit several families of relatively Sidorenko and relatively anti-Sidorenko oriented graphs. Despite the substantially stronger definitions, many known tournament Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko examples satisfy the relative inequalities, suggesting a broader theory of these phenomena in arbitrary host graphs and motivating several new structural and classification problems.

papers.name: On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields
papers.abstract: We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincaré half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $ω_r(x)-ω_r(y)$, where $ω_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point. We prove that two distinct separatrices which are not nested segments of the same straight line have a contact of order at most $4$ at a diagonal point and at most $2$ at a non-diagonal point. As a consequence, we obtain that the multiplicity of limit cycles in the double diagonalizable configuration is at most two, this bound being sharp.
